claims.text: Under conventional or standard cooling, Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 forms several primary non-eutectic crystalline phases.
Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 exhibits a multistep crystallization sequence during reheating.
Ultra-rapid cooling will suppress primary non-eutectic crystalline-phase formation during solidification.
Ultra-rapid cooling will increase the retained amorphous fraction.
Ultra-rapid cooling will improve thermal stability during subsequent reheating.
The cooling rate must exceed a critical rate for primary crystallization suppression.
The critical cooling-rate boundary is estimated to be approximately 10^6 K/s.
Extremely rapid quenching produces a lower density of crystallization seeds in the microstructure.
Rapid cooling minimizes atomic diffusion and rearrangement.
Minimized atomic mobility allows the alloy to bypass the kinetic window for primary-crystal formation.
A lower seed density promotes retention of the amorphous matrix.
A lower seed density delays the onset of crystallization during reheating.
Ultra-rapidly cooled samples will have a higher crystallization-onset temperature than slower-cooled samples.
Cooling rates below the critical boundary will continue to permit primary-phase formation.
The critical cooling rate and thermal-stability improvement depend on sample geometry and processing details.

contradictions.description: The conditions state that thermal analysis is performed below the conventional crystallization-onset temperatures, whereas the predicted outcome and experiment require heating through crystallization to measure the onset and exothermic peaks. This is contradictory unless 'below' means only the initial reheating temperature.
